Automated PR Cleanup

Thank you for contributing to opencode.

Due to the high volume of PRs from users and AI agents, we periodically close older PRs using automated criteria so maintainers can focus review time on the most active and community-supported contributions.

This PR was closed because it matched the following cleanup criteria:

- The PR was created more than 1 month ago
- The PR had fewer than 2 positive reactions
- Positive reactions are counted as thumbs-up, heart, celebration, or rocket reactions on the PR

PRs created within the last month are not affected by this cleanup.

If you believe this PR was closed incorrectly, or if you are still actively working on it, please leave a comment explaining why it should be reopened. A maintainer can review and reopen it if appropriate.

Thanks again for taking the time to contribute.

Still reproduces on **1.18.18** (`31406cc`) against a remote `opencode serve` opened in a browser. Confirming the exact seam for anyone triaging, since the fix is client-side:

- The sidebar renders the client-persisted list `store.projects[scope]` (`packages/app/src/context/server.tsx` L85), saved to `localStorage["opencode.global.dat:server"]` via `Persist.global` (`packages/app/src/utils/persist.ts`, `GLOBAL_STORAGE = "opencode.global.dat"`). "Add project" pushes into that same client store (server.tsx ~L110).
- Bootstrap *does* fetch the server's project list (`loadProjectsQuery` in `packages/app/src/context/global-sync/bootstrap.ts` ~L163), but only into the query cache — it never seeds the sidebar list. As #41156 puts it, `createServerProjects` reads only the client-side bookmark store, which is populated by user actions.

Net effect: a fresh browser/origin pointed at a server that already has projects shows an empty sidebar, and you have to re-"Add project" on every device even though `GET /project` returns them all.

Worth noting: the closely-related #41156 was closed as completed pointing at #41154, but #41154 is still open/unmerged — so this remains the live tracking issue. Fix direction that would close it: seed the sidebar from `GET /project` when the client list is empty (one-time hydrate), or make the project list server-owned.

The `exiting loop` followed by null-character blocks in your logs is the giveaway here, that's the TUI render loop dying, not a thermal or memory thing. Try running it headless with `opencode run` for a while, if the freeze stops that pins it to the WSLg/terminal renderer. Grab the debug log at freeze time too (`opencode --log-level debug`, then peek in `~/.local/share/opencode/log`) and see what is sitting right after `exiting loop`, that exact line is what the devs would need to isolate it.

## Additional findings

I performed a controlled comparison after my previous comment.

- A minimal request to `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses` using the same Go credentials and `gpt-5.6-luna` succeeds with HTTP 200.
- Replaying an old `reasoningEncryptedContent` stored in an affected OpenCode session reproduces the same HTTP 400 error:
  `invalid_encrypted_content`.
- Multiple existing sessions are affected, while fresh sessions work normally.
- The affected sessions contain opaque `reasoningEncryptedContent` and `itemId` metadata from previous Responses API outputs.
- The logs show connection resets/timeouts before the encrypted-content errors.

This appears to be related to stale or incompatible `reasoning.encrypted_content` being replayed when an existing session is continued. This is also related to the behavior described in #37444.

A possible fix would be for OpenCode to invalidate or omit opaque reasoning continuation metadata when the provider rejects it, then retry using the visible conversation history only. The UI should also provide a recoverable session error instead of leaving the existing session permanently unusable.

Same bug on Windows 11 with Orca IDE (xterm.js terminal, same as VS Code), opencode-ai 1.18.18 (npm global install).

Repro pattern: artifacts appear right after a task finishes / final output is rendered — leftover overlapping panels, garbled sidebar/status bar. The only reliable recovery is changing the tab zoom/scale in Orca (forces a grow resize → re-layout). Restarting the opencode session also recovers.

Additional data point for the maintainers:
- Terminal renderer is NOT the cause: I switched Orca's terminal from WebGL to DOM renderer (GPU Acceleration → Off, xterm.js DOM renderer) and the artifacts still appear. This is the OpenTUI stale-width/shrink issue, independent of the renderer.
- The shrink happens constantly in Orca (tab switches, panel layout changes after session end), so the bug is hit on every session completion.

Voting for the fix in PR #42474 / opentui PR #1363 to land — this makes opencode unusable-ish inside Orca on Windows.

Confirming this fix is needed: Windows 11 + Orca IDE (xterm.js-based terminal) + opencode 1.18.18 — stale-width artifacts appear on every session completion (leftover frames, garbled panels), recoverable only by forcing a grow-resize (changing tab zoom) or restarting opencode.

Tested and ruled out: switching the terminal to DOM renderer (Orca "GPU Acceleration" → Off) does NOT fix it — the issue is the TUI resize handling, not the renderer. Please land this.

I investigated this further, including the exact desktop beta build, and the evidence now points away from OpenCode configuration.

- `v0.0.0-beta-17639` was built by [workflow run 32213955302](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/32213955302) from source SHA [`6baad7fc3e15e1ff5859f43de62892052d4e6c32`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/6baad7fc3e15e1ff5859f43de62892052d4e6c32).
- In that build, the native OpenAI Responses lowering emits `prompt_cache_key` but has no code path that emits `prompt_cache_retention` or `prompt_cache_options` by default.
- I checked the complete 3.65 MB model snapshot embedded in that exact commit. It contains zero occurrences of those cache-control fields. The `gpt-5.6-sol-fast` mode only overlays `service_tier: "priority"`.
- The corresponding `models.dev` GPT-5.6 model history also never contained either field.
- An isolated control run using the pre-patch binary, an empty config, no external plugins, and no injected fields now succeeds against the same Codex endpoint.

The same failure occurred across multiple independent clients during the same time window, including the official Codex CLI and Codex Desktop. One official Codex reporter captured the generated request keys and confirmed that `prompt_cache_retention` and `prompt_cache_options` were both absent from the client request. OpenAI later confirmed the root cause directly: ["It was a server-side configuration issue."](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/39397#issuecomment-5346874374)

That also explains why this was intermittent, why it appeared after tool continuations, and why it is no longer reproducible with unchanged local configuration.

I have updated #43380 so it no longer closes this issue or claims to fix this incident. It is now scoped only as defensive transport-boundary hardening for cases where caller configuration or a plugin explicitly injects unsupported cache-control fields.

Notes on the setup:

- I never set `prompt_cache_retention` (or any provider/model options) anywhere: no `model`, `providers`, `agents`, or `plugins` keys in any config, no project `opencode.json(c)`, no opencode plugins. The `.claude`/`.agents` dirs only hold instruction/agent markdown.
- Model is picked in the desktop beta: `openai/gpt-5.6-sol-fast` with variant `max`.

About the sessions:

- Every failure is a **subagent** session (`explore`/`general`, spawned via the subagent tool from a desktop parent session). Session records all show the same model:

```json
{ "agent": "explore", "model": { "id": "gpt-5.6-sol-fast", "providerID": "openai", "variant": "max" } }
```

- Log has 15 occurrences total, all on 2026-08-19 between 06:42Z and 07:54Z, each `level=ERROR "Failed to drain Session" ... prompt_cache_retention is not supported on this model`, one per subagent session. None before or since.

Important: it's **not consistent** — sometimes it errors, sometimes it doesn't. I also can't reproduce it on demand:

- Sibling subagents in the same parent run, same model/variant, completed fine.
- The failing sessions themselves had successful model calls first (tool calls ran, tokens + cache reads recorded), then a later turn in the same session died with this error.

So it looks like something conditionally adds `prompt_cache_retention` (or upstream routing varies) on some subagent turns only. Happy to grab more logs with `OPENCODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` if it recurs — anything specific you'd want captured?

- #33356: Unbounded growth of the `event` table — `opencode.db` reaches 13GB+, mostly `message.updated.1` snapshots (no retention/compaction)

Confirmed on Linux x86_64 with OpenCode 2 preview `0.0.0-beta-17639`.

The `workspace.project_id` error is reproducible with a **fresh database**, so it is not database corruption or a legacy-schema-only problem:

1. Stop the service.
2. Move aside the existing OpenCode database files.
3. Run `opencode2 service start`.
4. The server logs `database schema bootstrap completed` with 44 migrations.
5. Inspecting the fresh DB shows `workspace` contains only `id, provider, binding, created_at, last_used_at`; there is no `project_id` column.
6. The server code subsequently queries `workspace.project_id` and fails with `SQLiteError: no such column: workspace.project_id`.

As a temporary local workaround, adding a nullable column makes the service usable:

```sql
ALTER TABLE workspace ADD COLUMN project_id TEXT;
```

After applying that workaround, restarting the service and running a minimal chat request completed successfully. This looks like a missing migration/schema definition in the beta rather than a corrupt user database.

Linux confirmation for the auto-update failure mode (OpenCode 2 preview `0.0.0-beta-17639`, Node 24.16.0, npm 12.0.2):

The background updater logged a successful command equivalent to:

```
npm install --global @opencode-ai/cli@0.0.0-beta-17639
```

but the installed `bin/opencode2.exe` was replaced by the package's 232-byte placeholder stub. New invocations failed immediately with:

```
Error: @opencode-ai/cli's postinstall script was not run.
```

This happened even though `npm config get ignore-scripts` returned `false`. An already-running service continued to work, making the breakage visible only after restart/new invocation.

Manual recovery was:

```
node <global-node-modules>/@opencode-ai/cli/postinstall.mjs
```

which restored the native executable and made `opencode2 --version` work. So this is not limited to Windows locking behavior; the updater should verify that postinstall produced a runnable binary before reporting success.
